summary: A two-model pair introduces a lossy protocol and correlated failure surface. A stronger plan can still be wrong, and a cheaper executor can convert a recoverable ambiguity into confident action.

points.text: Planner errors become upstream commitments: the executor may faithfully implement a flawed decomposition and never revisit the premise that produced it.
Different models may interpret schemas, tool semantics, uncertainty language, and domain terms differently; an apparently valid handoff can hide semantic mismatch.
A second model does not guarantee independent judgment. Related training data, shared prompts, and the first model's framing can cause correlated acceptance of the same error.
Two calls increase latency, telemetry, provider exposure, and operational complexity; for short or tightly coupled tasks a single well-instrumented model may be cheaper and more accurate.
